claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has relatively coarse grains.
The as-deposited coating has minimal grain-boundary oxide dispersion.
A targeted post-deposition heat treatment will refine the coating grain size.
The heat treatment will induce controlled formation of oxides at grain boundaries.
Refined grains produce a higher density of grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary oxide precipitates stabilize the refined grain-boundary structure.
The stabilized grain boundaries act as barriers to crack initiation.
The stabilized grain boundaries act as barriers to crack propagation.
The refined, oxide-stabilized structure enhances plastic accommodation through mechanisms such as grain-boundary sliding.
Enhanced plastic accommodation delays crack formation.
Delayed crack formation results in a lower wear rate.
Under sliding at 500°C or above, the heat-treated coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating.
Under sliding at 500°C or above, the heat-treated coating will deform more homogeneously than the as-deposited coating.
The heat-treated coating will exhibit increased plastic flow during high-temperature sliding.
The heat-treated coating will exhibit delayed crack initiation during high-temperature sliding.
The predicted effects are expected to hold at temperatures of at least 500°C under controlled sliding loads.
At lower temperatures or under different loading conditions, the effects of grain refinement and oxide dispersion may not be observable.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant wear-rate reduction and enhanced plastic-deformation indicators relative to the as-deposited control would falsify the hypothesis.
